content:
First, thanks for the help. i am up and running again (although not 100% satisfied with how)

I had read the link Matt provided. But he caused me to read it again. This time i noted the --allow-downgrade switch. Although i was NOT downgrading (same version on Windows and Linux), it offered a chance to avoid the erroneous exit. So i tried it. It worked.

Again in Wayne's reply, i AM NOT mixing versions. His comment about OS mixing is clear, and definative. But i hope the developers realize what a SIGNIFICANT LIMITATION this is.

I see Thunderbird's handling of Profiles as a weakness. My profile directory is 1 GB. It seems to contain almost 50 versions of pref.js. It mixes all kinds of information. IMHO there should be a clear separation between configuration info and state info. When i move to a new system (potentially a new OS), there is configuration info i NEED to take with me - Local Store of messages, account configs, address book, maybe calendar config, user settings. Then there is state info which does not need to be transportable - caches, telemetry histories, etc.

I see my usage as entirely reasonable and probably common. Multiple networked computers sharing a file system, where the computers have different OSes. It is desirable that my email functionality is independent of which computer i'm using today (never using multiple at once). In recognition of Matt's reply, i have now created separate Windows and Linux versions of my Profile. i see this as a kludge i must manage (unfortunately), and as a workaround of Thunderbird's deficient capability. I hope the Thunderbird team will consider tackling OS independence of the configuration file stores.
